question: In Microsoft Word, where do I go to set my own page margins instead of using a preset?

config.context_selection: rank order, unique IDs, whole chunks only

answer: In Microsoft Word, to set your own page margins instead of using a preset, go to the Layout tab and select the Margins icon. From the drop-down menu, choose the Custom Margins option at the bottom. This will open a dialog box where you can adjust the margins to your desired measurements [3b0d5af459cdb898927e175429808f0a08c08fce01cb66e7b79cecb673be4a2e].

results.text: To adjust the margins of a page, go to the Layout tab. Select the Margins icon, and a drop-down menu will appear. The default margin is Normal (1 inch on all sides), but this can be adjusted via the prepopulated options, such as for different layouts with narrower margins. If you want to set your own margins, choose the Custom Margins option at the bottom of the drop-down menu. In the dialog box shown in Figure 3.7, notice how you can adjust the margins to be various measurements.

question: According to the Word layout guidance, which page orientation works best when a table or graph would not fit well on a vertical page?

config.context_selection: rank order, unique IDs, whole chunks only

answer: According to the Word layout guidance, the landscape orientation works best for documents with tables and graphs that would not fit well on a vertical page [c507bf8ca42f95992b2ceb8e356c17c99f22796ccac0f2ab03e489138bda50c7].

arguments.query: According to the Word layout guidance, which page orientation works best when a table or graph would not fit well on a vertical page?

events.query: According to the Word layout guidance, which page orientation works best when a table or graph would not fit well on a vertical page?

results.text: Page orientation refers to whether the page is vertical or horizontal. The default in Word is the vertical layout, called portrait orientation. This layout works best for everyday text documents, such as business reports and correspondence. The horizontal layout is known as landscape orientation, and works best for documents with tables and graphs that otherwise would not fit well on a vertical page.

question: Why might a team use double-spacing in a working Word document while collaborators are using Track Changes?

answer: A team might use double-spacing in a working Word document while using Track Changes because it allows for better visibility of the changes or edits. question: Why does the Word heading guidance advise against using color to indicate hierarchy levels?

config.context_selection: rank order, unique IDs, whole chunks only

answer: The Word heading guidance advises against using color to indicate hierarchy levels because it is neither logical nor accessible. Using color alone does not provide a clear rationale for why one level would be higher or lower than another, and it may not be accessible to users who are visually impaired or have other accessibility needs [1ed4a54741e20e44698887612d3a2038c8cb8aa6295927c3314d441645e42131].

question: In Microsoft Word, how does resolving a comment differ from deleting it?

config.context_selection: rank order, unique IDs, whole chunks only

answer: In Microsoft Word, resolving a comment differs from deleting it in that deleting a comment removes it completely from the document, while resolving a comment retains the comment in a history stored digitally with the document. This allows the comment to be preserved for future reference even though it is no longer active in the document itself [d2444d18dd2ee3addabf5646a6bfaeae2dd67fffcef7912ffc14e92443d35daf].

question: In Word, why should body text and headings be assigned styles before applying a document theme?

config.context_selection: rank order, unique IDs, whole chunks only

answer: In Word, body text and headings should be assigned styles before applying a document theme because styles act as "codes" that tell Word how to format various sections of the document. These codes indicate which parts of the text are body text, titles, subtitles, etc. Without these style codes, the theme won't know how to apply itself to the document effectively. Assigning styles ensures that the theme can be applied to its full capacity, affecting fonts, font sizes, and colors consistently across the document [77ac78b5f17f74ca08c1a5331b0614306dbed9ba83fde8495d4f0fdc4ef52d54] [a07ae04c1c78db52862e80dc7c83421ae6a546fcda8e2b64420d6c630cb9c137] [e11fe753c964b68626110940ca20426586a00a22c83354712341fbd0c41dde69].

question: In Google Docs, how does applying heading styles affect the document outline as a heading hierarchy is built?

config.context_selection: rank order, unique IDs, whole chunks only

answer: In Google Docs, applying heading styles affects the document outline by adding the styled text to the outline pane on the left. As you apply styles within a hierarchy, the document outline reflects this hierarchy, making it easier to manage and navigate long documents. For example, when a heading style is applied to a section like "Industry and Market Analysis," it appears in the document outline as a heading, helping to organize the document's structure visually and functionally [41f5fa309109c033cf289cc4d1503bd10f21695983db84b1e2645e2b25faba2b].

As you continue to apply styles within a hierarchy, the outline in the document pane will reflect that hierarchy. For example, you can see that “Industry and Market Analysis” is now listed on the outline as a heading. This can be particularly useful when managing long documents, which Document Preparation covers.

question: In Google Docs, I want to move an entire paragraph to the right rather than indent only its first line. Which command should I use?

config.context_selection: rank order, unique IDs, whole chunks only

answer: To move an entire paragraph to the right in Google Docs, you should click anywhere in the paragraph, go to the Format menu, hover over "Align & indent," and then select "Increase indent." [1e7219ea9c285d741230328de53c84a986ef96ad5c886bed03fe8d66e7438d66]

results.text: To indent a body of text, the first line of the selection is indented to the right five spaces, which is the convention for indenting the first line of a paragraph. To do this indentation, press the Tab key on your keyboard. But if you want to move the entire paragraph to the right, click anywhere in the paragraph and go to the Format menu, then hover over Align & indent, and lastly, select Increase indent (Figure 3.47).

results.text: Docs also makes aligning and indenting text simple. If you want to align many paragraphs, just select them all together with the mouse, and then follow the same steps.
